MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 9, 2021
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:00 p.m., on March 9, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on March 4, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph (4) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 cases)

City Council Minutes  1  March 9, 2021
 CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Stein Mart Property 25282 Marguerite
  Parkway; Agency Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, Keith Rattay, Elaine Lister, Cheryl
  Dyas and William Curley. Negotiating Party: Kinstler Family Trust. Under
  Negotiation-Price and Terms.

CS3. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator
  is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council was updated on all three Closed Session items
but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize 2020 Orange County Fire Authority’s Mission Viejo Employee of the Year
  Thomas Olvera

  Mayor Kelley and Battalion Chief Eric Bennett recognized Firefighter Thomas Olvera.

P2. School Spotlight - Los Alisos Intermediate School

  Received presentation from Principal Richard Freda.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Lou Desimone, M.V.: Expressed concerns regarding the closure of Cordillera Elementary School
and the merger with Montevideo Elementary School. He felt that Saddleback Valley Unified
School District did not give public input and was not transparent.

Frederick Griefer, M.V.: Supports the Core Vision Plan and encouraged the City Council to forge
ahead with the project.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Asked in the name of transparency that the Council preserve the Oso Creek
Golf Course and Public Space Virtual Workshop Zoom Meeting and make it available for public
access. She questioned why the meeting was not being livestreamed.
City Council Minutes  2  March 9, 2021
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of February 23, 2021 as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated February 12, 2021 in the Amount of $2,503,496.16

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3  Check Register Dated February 19, 2021 in the Amount of $371,357.91

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2021

  Received and filed.

5.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for January 2021

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for January 2021

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January
  2021

  Received and filed.

8.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Second Quarter 2020/21

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  March 9, 2021
 9.  Los Alisos Boulevard, Marguerite Parkway, and Santa Margarita Parkway Pavement
  Rehabilitation Project (CIP 21837)

  Authorized issuance of a purchase order for design services for the subject project to Joseph
  C. Truxaw & Associates, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $77,600.

10. Alicia Parkway, Jeronimo Road, and Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation
  Project (CIP 20837) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

11. 2020 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 21838)-Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

12. Barcelona Walls - Intersections of Alicia Parkway and Muirlands Blvd. and Alicia
  Parkway and Charlinda Drive (CIP 330)

  Approved the Plans and Specifications and authorize staff to advertise for bids for the
  construction of two Barcelona walls at the intersection of Alicia Parkway and Muirlands Blvd.
  and Alicia Parkway and Charlinda Drive.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

PUBLIC HEARINGS

13. Ordinance to Allow and Regulate Residential Beekeeping in the City of Mission Viejo

  Planning and Economic Development Manager Larry Longenecker presented the staff report.

  Mayor Kelley opened the Public Hearing at 6:49 p.m.

  The following provided written comments in favor of the ordinance: Alexandra Berk, Maya
  Cappellino, April Hay, and Liane Linderman.

City Council Minutes  4  March 9, 2021
   Robin Jones: provided written comments to the Council to consider science-based requests
  that she outlined with respect to best practices that support public safety for bees and
  beekeeping.

  The following called in to voice in favor of the ordinance: Pamela Fraser, Laguna Hills and
  Liz Savage, Fullerton.

  Jerry Bryant, M.V.: called to voice his opposition of the ordinance.

  Mayor Kelley closed the Public Hearing at 7:11 p.m.

  Council Members asked various questions to staff and the City Attorney.

  Mayor Kelley suggested more public outreach to residents before this item returns.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs to table this
  item in order for staff to conduct further research on the type of bees and a certification
  program or educational/training component on beekeeping to be included in the ordinance.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  Kelley
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

14. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Sachs.

15. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

16. Economic Development Committee Update

  Council Member Sachs announced on Thursday, March 11f from 6:00 to 7:30 p.m. the Economic
  Development Committee will be hosting he Oso Creek Golf Course and Public Space Virtual
  Workshop. He encouraged residents to sign up via the City’s website to provide input.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

City Manager Dennis Wilberg announced that Mark Nix and Keith Rattay are working hard on
plans to extend the hours on all recreation centers. He stated that next week the County will be in
the red tier and a lot of the matrix are trending toward the orange tier. The key is the ability to hire
additional lifeguards to expand the hours of operation for our pools. The city is looking also for
opportunities for outdoor activities at the senior center.
City Council Minutes  5  March 9, 2021
 CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

City Attorney Bill Curley commented that the City is putting as much attention in trying to advance
our discussions regarding the Stein Mart project. All real estate deals move at their own speed but
wanted to assure the Council and community are focusing on the discussions.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

17. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell mentioned the Governor’s allowing for youth sports to begin again is
very exciting. He announced that the Marguerite Aquatics Center will be hosting the Tyr Pro Series
Swim Meet April 8 through April 11, which will include American Olympians that will compete in
the Summer Olympics in Tokyo. Council Member Goodell said that there will also be a high-level
diving competition as well in the near future. The Olympic Promotion Committee has continued
to meet and he looks forward to when Saddleback College can host events at their new stadium.
Lastly, he reminded residents of a blood drive on March 19 and next Tuesday March 16 there will
be a virtual Fair Housing Workshop.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths stated that it has been a long year for all the businesses. He mentioned that
he spoke with a friend that is a nurse at Mission Hospital and she stated that they have shut down
their expanded COVID unit and just have a handful of patients right now. He hopes that this is the
light at end of the tunnel. Lastly, he said he is excited for the youth sports to start again.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs stated it’s exciting to see that we are pushing the COVID behind us. He
looks forward see the City back up and operating and seeing people without having to wear a mask.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum encouraged residents to support the local high schools in their athletic
fundraisers. She stated that Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) voted as a
body for the housing allocations that were sent down from the State. Mission Viejo has been
assigned 2,117 housing units in the next eight years and it needs to be planned for this year in the
City’s General Plan. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum indicated that she was not at the meeting when the
vote was taken for the final allocations as she had a family situation out of state but would have
voted no if she had been at the meeting. She disagreed with the allocations were conducted was
City Council Minutes  6  March 9, 2021
 not done transparently. Announced that the Norman P. Community Center will be hosting a food
drive benefiting Families Forward. She also announced that there will be a shredding event at City
Hall on March 27. She encouraged residents to attend the Oso Creek Golf Course and Public Space
Virtual workshop on March 11. Lastly, she congratulated Tommy Olvera on being named Orange
County Fire Authority’s Mission Viejo employee of the year.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley announced that Saddleback Church Career Coaching Ministry is partnering with
Orange County Community Resources to host a South County virtual job fair on Wednesday April
7, 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Employers must advertise at least on payed fulltime regular position and
she encourages employers to register. Mayor Kelley said that employers may contact her directly
or they can go to oconestop.com/jobfairs to register. She commends Saddleback Church and Todd
Kaylish for wanting to help others during this difficult time. Mayor Kelley stated that over the
weekend she stumbled upon Eagle Scout Michael Hay along with members Troop 1210 at Pavion
Park working on extending the rail fencing along the park. She thanked him as well as city employee
Brian Zahn. She also attended a ribbon cutting event for Compass Bible Institute in Aliso Viejo this
past Sunday. She mentioned that she is waiting to receive her second vaccine at Soka University
and she encourages residents to sign up through the Othena App. She reminded residents that the
Saddleback Valley Unified School Board will be voting on the closure of Cordillera Elementary
School and merging those students to Montivideo Elementary School sometime this week and
encouraged those affected by this closure to reach out to the District for more information. Lastly,
she congratulated Firefighter Tommy Olvera being named Employee of the Year.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:21 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, March 23, 2021, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 23, 2021

City Council Minutes  7  March 9, 2021
